correctness.rationale: All legal square-sequence graph attachments of length <=4 are either edge attachments introducing 2 vertices and 3 edges or corner attachments introducing 1 vertex on an existing 2-edge path. Iterating both and removing exact graph-isomorphic duplicates gives 1,2,7,29 classes for lengths 1..4. For each, the forbidden independent 4-sets generate all nonfaces of Cliq_4; exhaustive nonempty face-poset Morse matchings directed along Hasse covers have exactly one critical 0-cell and only critical 5-cells (or none). Independent graph-isomorphism enumeration and a separately programmed full acyclicity check reproduced all 39 homotopy outcomes, including the s=4 distribution {(7,0):3,(8,0):4,(8,1):4,(9,2):7,(9,3):2,(9,4):1,(10,4):8}. Forman matching yields actual integral wedge S5 rather than mod-two homology only. Bound s<=4 essential.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS with clearly separated known all-edge subfamily: Filakovský 2602.11365 proves k=2,3 for corner sequences and arbitrary k for edge-only sequences, and conjectures corner-glued general k. The novel finite sector is k=4, at most 4 squares, including 21 corner-containing s=4 graph types; the 8 all-edge length-four types are already covered. No earlier exact 39-class/corner table was identified.
residual_risks: An unindexed exhaustive square-sequence computation could already classify the 21 corner-containing graph types.
Known all-edge cases (8 at s=4) are included for completeness and should never be described as newly obtained from scratch.
